Topic 8.1: Listening and speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Parts of the Body Suggested vocabulary head, hand, leg, eye, ear, nose, neck, fi in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: What do you do when someone is talking to you? 2. What is likely to happen if you pronounce a word wrongly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learning independently is enhanced as the learner work on their own to practise matching learnt vocabulary to pictures.

Values:
Respect: is enhanced as the learner appreciates other’s opinions in group/pair work

Responsibility: is developed as the learner works hard in pairs or groups to accomplish certain tasks.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Self-awareness is nurtured as the learner develops knowledge about the parts of their body.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities as learners pronounce words with the target sounds correctly for communication.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Audio recordings, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital

devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
